# Q3 study: outliers, sparsity, variation in scale (dataset C, 6-bit)

formats.py v3.0, weights only quantized, X in full precision, held-out Y error (odd X_cal columns), mean of 10 seeds. Margin = runner-up − winner in percentage points, mean ± sd over seeds; '(s/10)' = seeds in which that format won. Last column: how often the chosen selection method (exact sketch, activation-weighted, fitted on the even columns) picks the held-out class-rule winner.

Unmodified W_C, class rule: E3M2 5.469, E2M3 3.101, E4M1 11.149, MXINT6 4.054, BFP6 4.054, BFP6_g16 (cmp.) 3.484; selector picks E2M3.

## 3. Variation in scale

Gains 10^U(−a, a) applied (a) per **row** (one gain per output row: every block lies inside one row, so its scale absorbs the gain), (b) per **column** (input channel: gains change inside every block). 'weak 25%' = error of the Y rows with the 25% smallest gains (row mode), or of the part of Y coming from the 25% of input columns with the smallest gains (column mode). Last column: blocks whose 4-bit exponent clamps, BFP6 (out of 400) / BFP6_g16 (out of 700).
